measurement_notes.backend_cpu_ms: CPU time of the EcoCompute backend process (orchestration + validation), not model compute
measurement_notes.gpu_utilization: not observable: Nebius Token Factory is a serverless API and exposes no GPU telemetry
measurement_notes.gpu_memory: not observable through a serverless API
measurement_notes.measured_energy: not available: no power readings; energy is a FLOPs-based estimate

diagnosis.finding: Classification tasks use far fewer output tokens than the current 2048 token cap, indicating over‑provisioning of model size and token budget.
diagnosis.evidence: mean_completion_tokens=95.5, max_completion_tokens=144, mean_reasoning_tokens=92.2 (total avg generated ≈188 tokens) << 2048 cap; all 4/4 tasks passed on large tier.

diagnosis.finding: Extraction tasks have one failure despite low token usage, suggesting the current large tier may be unnecessary for most cases and a retry mechanism could recover the failed case without always paying the large‑tier cost.
diagnosis.evidence: mean_completion_tokens=287.5, max=368, mean_reasoning_tokens=248.0 (total avg generated ≈536 tokens) << 2048 cap; 3/4 tasks passed on large tier, 1/4 failed; cost per task ≈0.0010 USD.

proposals.rationale: Classification tasks generate <200 tokens total; a medium‑sized model provides sufficient capacity at lower per‑token cost.
proposals.evidence: mean_completion_tokens=95.5, mean_reasoning_tokens=92.2 → ~188 generated tokens per task; all 4/4 passed on large tier.
proposals.expected_effect: Reduce per‑task cost for classification by ~65% (medium tier is ~0.3× large tier for both input and output) while preserving latency within acceptable bounds.
proposals.risk: If any classification task requires deeper reasoning than medium can provide, it could fail; monitor validation pass rate after change.

proposals.rationale: The observed maximum output tokens is 144; a 256 token cap eliminates wasteful token budget without risking truncation.
proposals.expected_effect: Lower maximum token allocation, decreasing potential idle compute and slightly reducing latency; cost impact minimal because actual token usage stays below cap.
proposals.risk: Negligible; cap is comfortably above observed maximum.

proposals.rationale: Extraction tasks average ~536 generated tokens; a medium tier can handle this volume at substantially lower cost, with escalation to recover any failures.
proposals.evidence: mean_completion_tokens=287.5, mean_reasoning_tokens=248.0 → ~536 generated tokens per task; 3/4 passed on large tier.
proposals.expected_effect: Cut per‑task cost for extraction to ~30% of large‑tier cost for the majority of tasks; escalation will allow the failed task to retry on large tier if needed.
proposals.risk: Medium tier might be insufficient for some extraction cases, causing additional validation failures; escalation mitigates this by retrying on large tier.

proposals.rationale: Allow a fallback to the next larger tier when the validator rejects an answer, recovering the single failed extraction task without always using large tier.
proposals.evidence: 1/4 extraction tasks failed under current large‑tier-only configuration; enabling escalation gives a second chance on large tier after a medium‑tier attempt.
proposals.expected_effect: Recover the failed extraction task while keeping the majority of extraction tasks on the cheaper medium tier, lowering overall cost.
proposals.risk: Extra latency and cost for the retried task; however only one task is expected to trigger escalation based on current data.

proposals.rationale: Observed max output tokens is 368; a 512 token cap provides safe headroom while avoiding excessive unused token budget.
proposals.expected_effect: Reduce unnecessary token allocation, marginally lowering compute and latency for extraction tasks.
proposals.risk: Low; cap safely above observed maximum.
